name: Familial Amyloid Polyneuropathy

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic transthyretin (TTR) gene mutation
Presence of progressive peripheral sensorimotor polyneuropathy
Demonstration of amyloid deposits in tissue biopsy (nerve, fat pad, or organ)
Positive family history of amyloidosis or neuropathy
Evidence of cardiac amyloidosis by imaging or biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Pathogenic TTR mutation plus clinical evidence of progressive peripheral neuropathy and amyloid deposition on biopsy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential; biopsy may be omitted if genetic and clinical findings are definitive.

searchTerms: gradual numbness and weakness in limbs

pathognomonic.notes: Includes gastrointestinal dysmotility and erectile dysfunction

searchTerms: protein deposits found in tissue biopsy

common.symptomName: Cardiac conduction abnormalities and restrictive cardiomyopathy
searchTerms: heart rhythm problems and stiff heart muscle
abnormal heart conduction and restrictive cardiomyopathy

common.symptomName: Gastrointestinal symptoms including diarrhea and constipation
searchTerms: stomach and bowel issues like diarrhea and constipation
digestive symptoms including irregular bowel movements
GI problems with diarrhea and constipation

common.symptomName: Sensory loss in a stocking-glove distribution
searchTerms: tingling in gloves and socks area
loss of muscle strength and size
brain bleeding due to amyloid in blood vessels
brain vessel bleeding related to amyloid deposits

laboratory: Elevated serum TTR levels may be normal or decreased
Biopsy with Congo red staining showing apple-green birefringence under polarized light
imaging: Cardiac MRI showing late gadolinium enhancement consistent with amyloid infiltration
Nerve conduction studies demonstrating axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in the TTR gene, most commonly Val30Met
other: Fat pad aspirate or nerve biopsy positive for amyloid deposits
Autonomic function testing showing impaired sympathetic and parasympathetic responses

distinguishingFeatures: Demyelinating features on nerve conduction studies
Light chain (AL) amyloidosis with monoclonal gammopathy
Different amyloid protein type on biopsy
More prominent cardiac and renal involvement
Absence of amyloid deposits and TTR mutations

redFlags: Rapidly progressive sensorimotor neuropathy with autonomic failure
Family history of early-onset neuropathy or amyloidosis
Cardiac conduction abnormalities in a young patient
references: Ando Y, Coelho T, Berk JL, et al. Guideline of transthyretin-related hereditary amyloidosis for clinicians. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2013;8:31.
Plante-Bordeneuve V. Familial amyloid polyneuropathy. Curr Opin Neurol. 2018;31(5):529-535.
Sekijima Y. Transthyretin-related familial amyloid polyneuropathy: pathogenesis and therapeutic strategies. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry. 2015;86(9):1036-1043.
